title: Half of Customer Service Jobs Gone by 2030 — Here's Your Move
metaDescription: Forrester says 49% of customer service jobs vanish by 2030. The smart ones are already learning AI. Here's what they figured out.
author: Marty @ CertFlo

sections.heading: The Numbers Just Dropped
sections.body: So Forrester's research came out and it's wild. 49% of customer service jobs gone by 2030. AI is already handling 90% of stuff at Heathrow Airport and 96% at Anthropic. CMSWire covered it this week. But here's the thing everyone's missing: This isn't happening TO people. It's happening FOR the ones who see it coming. You're reading this, which means you're already ahead of like 90% of people who just scroll past this stuff. The shift is happening whether you join it or not. Question isn't if AI's gonna reshape customer service. Question is whether you'll be the one using it.

sections.heading: The People Who Stayed
sections.body:
Think about those Heathrow and Anthropic numbers for a second. These companies didn't just replace humans with machines. They figured out how to make humans way more capable with AI.

The customer service people who stuck around aren't handling basic questions anymore. They're solving the complex stuff, managing AI systems, doing the high-touch work that actually needs a person. They're not customer service reps anymore — they're like customer experience architects or whatever.

Same pattern everywhere. People who learn to work WITH AI become more valuable. People who ignore it become replaceable. That's it.

sections.heading: Your Move
sections.body:
The smart ones in customer service are already building AI skills. Learning prompt engineering. Getting good at AI workflow automation. Becoming the people their companies can't function without.

While everyone else is worried about AI taking over, these people are taking over AI. They're getting promoted. Writing their own job descriptions. They're gonna be managing the AI systems that their old coworkers couldn't figure out.

It's not humans versus AI. It's humans who get AI versus humans who don't. And that gap is getting wider every day.

Here's the thing: By 2030, being "good with AI" won't be special. It'll be basic. The customer service people who start now get six years to pull ahead of everyone else.

sections.heading: Window's Open
sections.body: You can spend the next few years watching AI reshape your industry from the sidelines. Or you can spend them learning the systems that'll define the next decade. Companies rolling out AI customer service need people who understand both the tech and the human side. They need people who can design AI workflows, train systems, handle the complex cases that actually need expertise. These aren't minimum-wage jobs. These are the high-value roles companies will pay serious money to fill. But only if you have the skills they need.
